items.title: Makai week 47: clean tanker spot earnings down 4.8% w/w, led by Atlantic MRs
items.summary: Makai Research's Nov 19 product tanker report shows clean spot earnings down 4.8% week on week and 13.4% below the late-October peak. Atlantic MR earnings fell most while Pacific MRs held steady; LRs slipped 2.1% and Handies were the only class to gain, on Med/Med. On the dirty side, Suezmax and Aframax spot earnings are 71% and 56% below their mid-October peaks.

items.title: TORM board rejects Hafnia's all-share merger proposals
items.summary: TORM's board unanimously turned down Hafnia's conditional all-share proposals on Nov 18, saying they undervalued TORM and offered no real control premium; TORM puts its NAV at $39.60/share as of Sept 30 and guides 2026 TCE earnings of $1.75–1.90bn. Hafnia, which holds about 19.8% of TORM, expects to decide by Nov 25 whether to distribute those shares (one TORM share per 26.3 Hafnia shares) or pay a cash dividend.

items.title: Jones Act waiver renewed for a third 90-day term, to Feb 14, 2027
items.summary: The White House extended the Jones Act waiver, first issued on March 17, for another 90 days from Nov 16; cargo must be loaded on an authorized vessel by 11:59 p.m. ET on Feb 14, 2027. The Offshore Marine Service Association, representing 170 companies, objected to the waiver entering its ninth month.

items.title: Signal Ocean: US Gulf crude loadings ease to ~3.1m b/d; Aframax list shortens
items.summary: Signal Ocean's week 46 monitor shows all 16 dirty routes lower between Nov 6 and 13, with TD22 (USG–China VLCC) down 44.1% to $232,000/day and TD3C down 17.9% to $1.06m/day. Provisional US Gulf crude loadings averaged about 3.1m b/d for Nov 1–12 versus about 4.0m b/d in October; the USG Aframax list was 39 ships on Nov 14 (about 50 in September) and West of Suez Aframax/LR2 laden counts rose 2.3% to 367.7.

items.title: CIMC SOE wins 10 MR tankers from Stamford Shipping
items.summary: Nantong CIMC Sinopacific Offshore & Engineering said on Nov 16 that Singapore's Stamford Shipping ordered ten 49,900 dwt MR product tankers, with an unnamed European owner taking two more of the same design. Price and delivery schedule were not disclosed.

items.title: EU lists 101 entities and Sovcomflot in shadow-fleet sanctions round
items.summary: The European Council designated 12 individuals and 101 entities tied to Russia's shadow fleet, including ship managers, traders and insurer Balance Insurance, with Sovcomflot listed as an associated entity. Designated firms are based in the UAE, China, Seychelles and Oman, and the tanker Garuda was named.

items.title: INTERTANKO, IPTA and seven other bodies urge global GHG rules before MEPC 85
items.summary: Nine industry associations including INTERTANKO, IPTA, BIMCO and ICS called on governments to agree a global decarbonisation framework as soon as practicable, ahead of the IMO environment committee meeting in London Nov 30–Dec 4. They oppose regional or national measures that duplicate compliance or charge twice for the same emissions, and ask for flexible compliance and guidance on fuel certification and lifecycle emissions.

items.title: UKMTO reports two more tankers hit near Khasab on Nov 21
items.summary: UKMTO said one tanker was struck at the stern about 20 km north of Khasab and another in the engine room about 31 km east of Khasab on Saturday; no casualties were reported and it is unclear whether two separate ships were involved. Iranian state TV said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine east of the strait while sailing with AIS off; that claim has not been independently verified.

items.title: CENTCOM extends Iran blockade to ship-to-ship transfers
items.summary: A Nov 18 US Central Command advisory says vessels taking cargo at sea from Iran-loaded ships may be treated as blockade evaders and can be stopped, boarded, diverted or seized. The blockade was imposed Apr 13, lifted in June and reimposed Jul 14; Iranian crude exports are reported to be near a standstill.

items.title: Lloyd's List: October Hormuz transits highest since the war began
items.summary: Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 550 non-Iranian-linked Hormuz transits in October (504 in September), 442 of them tankers and gas carriers, plus 106 Iranian-linked transits (83 in September). UKMTO has logged 163 events since the conflict began, including seven attacks Nov 5–11, and 10% of vessels reported attacked since mid-August have been confirmed lost or sunk.

items.title: Outbound tanker hit in engine room 6 nm north of Khasab (UKMTO 212-26)
items.summary: UKMTO reported an unidentified tanker leaving the strait was struck in the engine room by an unknown projectile at 1645 UTC on Nov 18, about 6 nm north of Khasab. Crew were reported safe; damage and any pollution were not known. The alert was issued early Nov 19 after a delayed report from local authorities.

items.title: Lower Mississippi at New Orleans restricted to one-way traffic through Dec 11
items.summary: The Coast Guard set a safety zone at river miles 95.5–96.5, extending 500 ft from the east bank near the Crescent City Connection, to salvage the river cruise ship American Heritage, which capsized after the tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck it on Nov 13. The alternate channel is closed, and deep-draft ships and tows of 10 or more barges are limited to one-way transits under the main span, possibly until Dec 11.

items.title: LA/Long Beach watchmen reach tentative deal; strike averted
items.summary: The Pacific Maritime Association said on Nov 21 it reached a tentative agreement, under federal mediation, with ILWU Local 26 covering about 250 watchmen at six container terminals, after the contract deadline of 12:01 a.m. that day. The current contract is extended pending member ratification; terms and timing were not disclosed. PMA's prior offer included a $3,200 one-time bonus and average pay rising from about $170,000 to $198,000.

items.title: S&P 500 −3.7% to 6,910.39 Friday; S&P and Dow enter correction (Nov 20)
items.summary: Friday's close: S&P 500 −265.44 (−3.70%) at 6,910.39, Dow −949.73 (−1.93%) at 48,147.33, Nasdaq −1,261.47 (−5.28%) at 22,617.73, as selling in AI-related shares continued and Anthropic's post-IPO gains faded. It was the S&P 500's seventh straight loss, its longest streak since February 2020; for the week the S&P fell 8.61%, the Dow 8.02% and the Nasdaq 10.02%, and the Nasdaq is now down for 2026. The VIX closed at 35.89.
items.source: Reuters via Yahoo Finance / The Closing Print

items.title: Nvidia −14% amid reports of SEC accounting review and California subpoena
items.summary: Nvidia closed at $125.53, down about 14% on Nov 20. Reports cited in market wraps said SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues and that California's attorney general issued an investigative subpoena over whether its chips reached China; neither the company nor regulators had confirmed these reports in the sources reviewed.

items.title: Brent settles $92.57, WTI $83.98 Friday; third weekly decline (Nov 20)
items.summary: Brent rose 0.64% to $92.57 and WTI 0.93% to $83.98 on Friday on Iran-related risk, but both posted a third straight weekly loss (WTI about −5.6% on the week). Reuters attributed the weekly decline to strong Middle East export flows, with Hormuz crude shipments near pre-war levels adding to surplus expectations. A Henry Hub settle was not available in the sources reviewed.

items.title: 10-year yield 4.92%, down 23 bp on the week; dollar index 103.84 (Nov 20)
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield fell 12 bp to 4.92% on Friday, from 5.15% a week earlier, and the 2-year fell 13 bp to 4.63%, as investors moved into bonds. The dollar index was little changed at 103.84 and up 0.42% for the week; gold fell about 4%.

items.title: Markets price Fed hikes in December and January; Waller raises 50 bp option
items.summary: Futures pricing still reflects a 25 bp Fed rate increase at the December meeting and another in January. Governor Christopher Waller said a 50 bp move could be considered in December; minutes of the October FOMC, released Nov 18, showed nearly all officials expected further increases would likely be needed.

items.title: Kushner says Russia appears open to NATO-style guarantees for Ukraine
items.summary: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff briefed nearly 40 European leaders in Berlin; Kushner said Moscow seems willing to accept postwar security guarantees modelled on NATO's Article 5 and that Trump is open to them if they serve US interests. The form of any guarantee and whether Kyiv and Moscow would agree remain unclear; the Kremlin has invited European officials to Moscow, with no date set.

items.title: Zelensky wants concrete agenda for next four-party talks; seeks all-for-all POW swap
items.summary: Speaking in Kyiv on Nov 21 with UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, Zelensky said the next round of talks among Ukraine, Europe, Russia and the US needs a clear agenda with minimum and maximum goals, and that timing depends on Washington. He welcomed the Abu Dhabi agreement to exchange more than 1,000 Ukrainian prisoners and called for an all-for-all exchange. He also said Trump told European leaders on Nov 19 they were spending heavily on Ukraine, which he said did not sound like a threat.

items.title: Putin rules out Black Sea and energy truce after third strike on Kerch Bridge
items.summary: After Ukraine hit the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge for the third time in a week, Putin said Russia would no longer consider a pause in strikes at sea or on energy facilities and said the damaged road section would be rebuilt. Each side reported overnight attacks; these casualty and interception figures have not been independently verified.

items.title: Houthi attack damages Saudi PIF tower in Riyadh
items.summary: Saudi authorities said a Houthi attack early Nov 19 damaged several floors of the Public Investment Fund tower and nearby buildings in Riyadh's financial district; the coalition said the damage came from debris after it intercepted four ballistic missiles and one cruise missile, while the Houthis claimed direct hits. Casualty reports were unclear, and the Houthi-run Saba agency reported Saudi airstrikes on Sanaa afterwards.

items.title: UK and EU leaders meet in Brussels on trade and carbon-market links
items.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham met Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa on Nov 20 to discuss a food and farm standards agreement (valued by London at up to £5.1bn a year), linking UK and EU carbon markets (up to £3.8bn a year) and a youth mobility scheme. The final outcome had not been confirmed in the sources reviewed.

items.title: IAEA: North Korea completes exterior of Yongbyon enrichment extension
items.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi told the agency's board that an extension to the Yongbyon uranium enrichment facility, under construction since mid-September, was externally complete by late October. The agency monitors the site by satellite because inspectors have been barred for years.

items.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea build up forces along their border
items.summary: Sources told Reuters both countries are massing troops along the border; the ACLED monitor reported clashes near Badme, which Reuters could not independently confirm.

items.title: Broncos (7–2) host Raiders Sunday 3:25 PM CT; Brandon Jones questionable
items.summary: Denver, tied with Kansas City (7–2) for first in the AFC West after its bye, hosts Las Vegas (4–6) on Sunday, Nov 22 at 3:25 PM CT on CBS. Friday's report lists TE Caleb Lohner (foot, on IR) out and S Brandon Jones (hamstring) questionable; Talanoa Hufanga, Jaylen Waddle and Riley Moss carry no game status. For the Raiders, DT Tonka Hemingway is out and TE Brock Bowers and K Matt Gay are questionable.

items.title: Texans 4–6 after 26–3 win; host Ravens Nov 29 at noon CT
items.summary: Houston beat Indianapolis 26–3 on Thursday, Nov 19, with C.J. Stroud throwing three touchdown passes and David Montgomery rushing for 107 yards. The Texans are second in the AFC South behind Jacksonville (7–2) and host Baltimore (4–6) on Sunday, Nov 29 at 12:00 PM CT on CBS; no new injury news was confirmed.

items.title: Alcaraz beats Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) to reach ATP Finals final
items.summary: Carlos Alcaraz came from a set down to beat Ben Shelton in Saturday's first semifinal in Turin, taking his head-to-head record to 5–1. He faces the winner of Alexander Zverev vs Daniil Medvedev (Medvedev qualified by beating Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 6-4), which starts no earlier than 1:30 PM CT Saturday; the final is Sunday, Nov 22.

items.title: Davis Cup Final 8 opens Tuesday in Bologna
items.summary: Quarterfinals: Czechia vs Canada (Tue Nov 24, 9:00 AM CT), Italy vs South Korea (Wed Nov 25, 9:00 AM CT), Great Britain vs Germany (Thu Nov 26, 3:00 AM CT) and Austria vs Spain (Thu Nov 26, not before 10:00 AM CT); the final is Sun Nov 29 at 8:00 AM CT. Zverev has already secured the 2026 year-end No. 1 ranking.
